hints: In the cars’ frame, the two cars are fixed points 5 km apart. How fast must the truck move in that frame to cover 5 km in 3 minutes?
worded:
1. The cars move together, so in their frame they are two fixed markers 5 km apart.

2. The truck goes from one to the other in 3 min = 1/20 h, so its speed relative to the cars is 5 × 20 = 100 km/h.

3. Moving opposite to the cars, its relative speed is its own speed plus 60. So the truck moves at 100 − 60 = 40 km/h. (A)
conventional:
![](asset:P000175-sol-1)

Relative speed of the truck with respect to the cars: $v + 60$ km/h. Covering 5 km in $\frac{3}{60}$ h:

$$(v + 60)\frac{3}{60} = 5\  \Rightarrow \ v + 60 = 100\  \Rightarrow \ v = 40\unit{km/h}.$$
mistakes: Opposite directions: relative speed is the sum (v + 60), not the difference.
Convert 3 min to hours (1/20 h) when speeds are in km/h.
